tiles.h3: Where the Wall Meets the Floor
tiles.body: Groundwater around the foundation. That's a drainage and sump pump issue.
Surface water from heavy rain, gutters or a yard that slopes toward the house.
A burst pipe, a water heater or a washer hose. Shut off the water and call.

blocks.intro: On July 11 and 12, 2017, 7.31 inches of rain fell at the gauge just south of Elgin, and basements flooded across the area.

items.body: Stone and block foundations in Elgin's oldest neighborhoods let groundwater in through joints and cracks during long wet spells.
Homes built before backflow protection was common have floor drains that connect straight to the sewer. In a big storm, that's where water rises.
Nearly 3 in 10 Elgin homes went up between 1990 and 2009, many with finished basements. Water there damages flooring, drywall and furniture fast.
A clear sewer line, a backflow valve, a [sump pump with a battery backup](/elgin/sump-pumps) and, for repeat backups, an [overhead sewer system](/elgin/overhead-sewer-systems).

bodies: Waterproofing keeps groundwater out of the basement. Our part is the plumbing behind it: sump pits and pumps, battery backups, discharge lines and the drain tile that carries water to the pit.

If water comes through the walls or where the wall meets the floor, the drain tile may be clogged or the pump may not keep up. We check the system and tell you what will stop the water. For water coming up through drains, see [sewage backup service](/elgin/sewage-line-backup-services).

blocks.h2: Basement Flooding Questions From Elgin Homeowners

items.q: What should I do first when my basement floods?
items.preview: Stay safe, stop the water if you can and call.
items.answer: Stay away from water near outlets or appliances. If it's from a pipe or appliance, shut off the main water valve. If it's coming up through the floor drain, stop using water in the house. Then call us.

items.q: Does a backflow valve stop basement flooding?
items.preview: It stops sewer water from coming in. It doesn't stop groundwater.
items.answer: A backflow valve stops sewer water from flowing back into your home through the drain. It doesn't stop groundwater. If you already have one and it failed, we can repair or replace it.

items.q: Why does my basement only flood in big storms?
items.preview: The sewer or the ground is overloaded.
items.answer: In a big storm, either the public sewer fills and pushes back through your floor drain, or groundwater rises faster than your sump pump can handle. We'll find out which.

items.q: Can old stone foundations be kept dry?
items.preview: Usually, with the right drainage and pump.
items.answer: Usually. Older foundations need good drain tile, a reliable sump system and surface water directed away from the house.

items.q: How much does it cost to fix basement flooding in Elgin?
items.preview: It depends on the source and the fix. You get a flat price first.
items.answer: It depends on where the water comes from and what it takes to stop it. We give you a flat-rate price for each option before any work begins.
